## Opponent Reads

**Player 2**: **LAG/maniac, extreme calling station postflop AS PFA.** Opens very wide (~50% PFR). 4-bets and 3-bets extremely wide — including with premiums (AA). **As PFA**: Calls down with virtually anything — including calling multi-street donk-leads with just overcards. C-bets most flops, checks dry/paired boards. Turn: AIR → checks/folds (float profitable); MEDIUM HANDS → checks turn, calls river (station mode); REAL HANDS → shoves aggressively. Folds to turn raises even after double-barreling. **As NON-PFA (BB defend, etc.)**: Fit-or-fold — folds to c-bets when whiffing. Stabs turn with marginal holdings but gives up river on scary boards. **DONK-LEADS with strong made hands (especially in 3-bet pots).** **CHECK-RAISES with semi-bluffs/draws on wet boards** — barrels turn with equity, CHECK-FOLDS river when draw misses. **Key line: P2 check-raise flop → bet turn → check river = BUSTED DRAW — attack with river bet.** Calls 3-bets with pocket pairs (including JJ). **SESSION 2 CONFIRMED: P2 accumulated chips consistently — LAG style thriving at this table. Now chip leader. Must find counter-lines.** **Exploit**: Flat opens IP with suited broadways/connectors. 3-bet QQ+/AKs only. Value bet extremely thin as PFA. Float flop c-bets. DO NOT bluff when P2 is calling with made hands. DO bluff when P2's line = busted draw. As 3-bet caller: c-bet when P2 checks (will fold air); FOLD to P2's donk-lead + turn aggression (strong).

**Player 3**: **Tight-aggressive, skilled — most dangerous opponent (~7% VPIP in raised pots). STICKIER THAN EXPECTED in limped/multiway pots** — completes SB wide, then calls down with weak pairs. 3-bets from blinds vs ALL positions. **Confirmed trapper — wide check-raise range** on wet boards in 3-bet pots. C-betting is SELECTIVE. Triple-barrels one-pair value. **Vs RAISED POTS with escalating pressure**: calls flop+turn then folds river to size. **Vs LIMPED/SMALL POTS: stickier — calls down light.** **SESSION 2: Bled chips significantly (finished $620). May be tilting or running bad — watch for widened ranges or frustration plays next session.** **Exploit**: Multi-street barrels work in raised pots. In limped pots, value bet wider. Good steal target in blinds.

**Player 4**: **Tight (~13% VPIP), passive preflop, EXTREME calling station.** Calls 3-bets with junk. Calls river with bottom pair, 9-high. PASSIVE with strong made hands — checks made straights through ALL streets. **3-bets are strong (JJ+/AQ+) but folds to 4-bets. 5-BET SHOVE includes JJ.** As single-raiser: C-bets flop, folds to turn raises — FLOATABLE. **As LIMPER: DOUBLE-BARRELS aggressively with draws, then GIVES UP on river when draw misses.** **Exploit**: 3-bet for VALUE only. Value bet extremely wide (#1 value target). NEVER bluff P4 when calling. Respect check-raises/donk-bets/limp-reraises/3-bets.

**Player 5**: **Very tight nit (~7% VPIP), sticky with pocket pairs.** C-bets flop then shuts down without connection. Donk-bets can be strong OR weak — weak ones fold to raises/turn barrels; strong ones ESCALATE. **ANY turn raise from P5 = monster.** **Exploit**: Two-barrel bluff donk-bets. Call flop c-bets wider. FOLD to P5's turn raises always. Good steal target in blinds.

**Player 6**: **Station/spewy — wide limper, opener, AND cold-caller. More competent than raw classification suggests.** **As LIMPER: EXTREMELY sticky postflop — calls with bottom pair. BUT folds preflop to large iso-raises.** **As COLD-CALLER: Donk-leads with AIR/weak draws → RAISE for fold equity. CHECK-CALLS with real made hands — passive line = actual hand.** Key tell: P6 donk-lead = air; P6 check-call = real hand. MASSIVE overbets = value. **4-bet shoves are NUTTED.** **Exploit**: Value bet wide. SIZE DOWN iso-raises (~3x) to keep P6 in. NEVER bluff check-calling P6. RAISE donk-leads (they're air). FOLD to 4-bet shoves/overbets.

**Player 7**: **Wide opener AND wide limper. EXTREMELY wide caller preflop — calls 3-bets AND 4-bets with suited junk (confirmed: 57s, QQ into 5-bet).** Cold-calls do NOT indicate premiums. Passive preflop, AGGRESSIVE postflop WITH STRENGTH. Checks flop with middle pair, waits for improvement, then value bets. Donk-leads and triple-barrels with strength. Checks down with air. **SESSION 2: Lost significant chips ($690). Short-stacked — may widen or gamble more.** **Exploit**: Iso-raise wide, value bet relentlessly and size up. Don't bluff postflop.

1. **LEVERAGE TIGHT IMAGE**: Widen steal attempts (35% VPIP from LP), add light 3-bets vs wide openers (P2, P6, P7). Fold equity is at a premium — use it before it decays.
2. **Thin value > bluffing** against stations (P2, P4, P6, P7). But image now supports more bluffs than before.
3. **Bluffing is LINE-BASED**: Target P2's busted draw line (CR→barrel→check); P4's lead-lead-check; weak P6 donk-leads.
4. **Counter P2's chip lead**: Don't avoid — engage with position. Flat IP with suited connectors/broadways, exploit their postflop tendencies. They're winning through volume; counter with positional play.
5. **Float P2 and P5 on flops** — both shut down on turn without hands.
6. **Multi-street barrels work vs P3 in RAISED pots**. In LIMPED pots, value bet wider.
7. **Never bluff P4 (station), sticky P6 (check-calling), P7 (aggressive with strength).**
8. **P3 and P7 are SHORT** — they may gamble/shove wider. Tighten calling ranges vs their all-ins, but steal from them more.
9. **Be cautious with KQ** — don't overcommit without strong board connection.
10. **SIZE DOWN iso-raises vs P6** (~3x) to keep them calling dominated.

**Threat hierarchy**: P2 (chip leader, LAG volume) > P3 (skilled, but short) > P6 (underestimated competence) > P7 (gambly, short) > P5 (tight/predictable) > P4 (exploitable station).
